predictive_glyph.reading: The W image and the I image are the same length, the same layout, and carry the same 31-character field width; nothing but the letter differs. Across 120 sampled frames they are bit-identical on 57 and differ on 63, every one of them localised, in two windows each bounded by bit-identical frames on both sides. Not one frame anywhere is diffuse -- which also explains the diffuse windows in the baseline comparisons: the retail names vary in length, the two synthetic ones do not, and it is that length difference that moves the game's own timing. Nothing but glyph rendering of the written bytes produces a residual that tracks which letter was written.

coverage.why_fixed_allocation_decides: A fixed-allocation lane rewrites bytes in place and changes no member's stored size, so the disc read schedule is untouched and the two runs stay in lockstep; the comparison is then exact equality outside the edit. A re-packing lane moves stored sizes, which moves the read schedule, which the spec measured turning into a different scene 59 seconds downstream. This column is measured off each lane object's own fixed_allocation attribute [M], and it is the column that decides the order of work.
